why_bad: One MSA that deliberately fails all five Day 5 checks: open third-party sharing, indefinite retention, no breach notice duty, no liability cap, and no return/delete on exit.

expected_findings.reason: Vendor may share personal data with any third party with zero customer notice or approval.

expected_findings.evidence_must_contain: as long as Vendor deems useful
expected_findings.reason: Retention is indefinite and deletion when no longer needed is expressly disclaimed.

expected_findings.evidence_must_contain: does not require Vendor to notify
expected_findings.reason: No customer notification duty or timing for a personal data breach.

expected_findings.evidence_must_contain: does not state any maximum liability
expected_findings.reason: No clear maximum payout / fees-based limitation of liability.

expected_findings.evidence_must_contain: no obligation to return or delete
expected_findings.reason: On exit, data may stay in backups forever with no return/delete duty.

expected_no_flag.reason: Fees are commercial terms unrelated to third-party data sharing.
Fees clause should not trigger retention findings.
Definitions alone are not a breach-notification gap.
